jobs.prompt: After swarm update the running board (swarm watch, and the remote board behind swarm remote serve) kept serving the old version (1.161.0) until the owner restarted it by hand. Make swarm update restart the running servers automatically, gracefully, on the same port and with the same flags, then confirm the new version. Registry: every server records itself at start. The board already writes a board file ({ pid, url, startedAt }, see tools/watch-cli.mjs near the boardFile writer): extend that record with version (the running package version), argv (the exact command line after the node runner, for example [watch, --all, --port, 4317]), cwd, port, a safe subset of the environment (only SWARM_* variables, HOME and PATH) and mode: terminal when stdin and stdout are TTYs, otherwise background. Add the same record for swarm remote serve (a new remote server file next to the board file, written and removed with the same atomic write and cleanup rules, mode 0600). The board server exposes its running version on a health route (add /api/health returning { ok: true, version, pid } if none exists, loopback only, no secrets). Restart (a new module tools/server-restart.mjs, called from the update flow in tools/swarm/core-52.mjs where swarm update finishes successfully, and also when swarm update finds it is already up to date but a recorded server runs an older version than the installed current): for each record whose pid is alive and whose version differs from the installed version: background mode: send SIGTERM, wait up to 15 seconds for the process to exit (never SIGKILL: if it is still alive after the wait, leave it and report it), wait until the port is free, start the replacement detached (stdio ignored, own session, unref) with the NEW runner (current/tools/swarm.mjs of the install root, resolved after the update) and the recorded argv, cwd and environment subset, then poll the health route (or the remote server file for swarm remote serve) every 250 ms for up to 20 seconds until it reports the new version; print one line per server: board restarted: 1.161.0 to 1.162.0 (port 4317, pid 1234), or remote server restarted: ..., or a clear failure line with the exact command to run by hand; a failed start is retried once; the old process is never left stopped without a report. Terminal mode (a server running in the owner's terminal): do NOT kill it; print board running in a terminal (pid N) still serves 1.161.0: press Ctrl-C there and run swarm watch ARGS again; and make the board show a banner restart needed: installed 1.162.0 (the server compares its start version with the installed current version when it answers /api/health and in the snapshot it serves; a small non-blocking banner in tools/watch-assets/board.js). Stale records (dead pid) are removed silently. The restart never runs during a swarm update that failed, never for a server whose record cannot be parsed (report it), never when swarm update is given --no-restart, and never for a pinned project (a pinned project does not own servers; ignore this clause if it has no meaning). The update result JSON gets a servers array: [{ kind, pid, from, to, port, status }] and the human output prints the lines above after the version line. Tests in tests/server-restart.test.mjs, hermetic (temp install root and HOME, small fake server scripts that write a record with the same shape and listen on a free port with a /api/health route, no real board, no network beyond loopback, no reading of the ambient environment): a background fake server is restarted (new pid, same port, same argv, new version reported by health, one confirmation line), a terminal-mode record is not killed and gets the message, a server that ignores SIGTERM for longer than the wait is reported and not killed, a replacement that fails to start is retried once and then reported with the manual command, a stale record is removed, an unparsable record is reported and skipped, --no-restart skips everything, no servers means no extra output, the remote server record works the same, up to date plus an old running server still restarts it, the health route returns the version, and the banner appears in the snapshot when the versions differ. Keep every existing test passing (tests/installed-swarm.test.mjs, update tests, watch and board tests, completion metadata: add the --no-restart flag to the help text and the command metadata). Do not break the import-cycle rule: tools/server-restart.mjs must not statically import install.mjs. No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: tests that reference swarm.mjs in passing are covered by the full suite run before merge.
